chunks: Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Bashshār al-Wāsiṭī, who said:
I wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام that I have a relative who has proposed to my daughter, and there is bad character in his conduct.
So he said: “Do not marry her to him if he is of bad character.”

key_terms.خَطَبَ: sought marriage or proposed for marriage

ai.seo_question: Can a daughter be married to someone who is known to have bad character?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام advised against marrying a daughter to a man known for bad character. It highlights moral character as an important consideration in marriage decisions within Islamic family law and ethics.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4428 - Yaqub ibn Yazid narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Bashshar Al-Wasiti, who said:
I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as) saying:
"I have a relative who has proposed to my daughter, but he has bad character."
Imam (as) replied: "Do not marry her to him if he has bad character."
